chapter: Henry Horton and the Rhythm Club
title: Henry Horton band, WJSU broadcasts and low pay
summary: Played with Horton's band at the Rhythm Club broadcasting nightly on WJSU for $1.40 a night, about 1937-38.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Must have been a bit of a big deal to broadcast then.

Well, he was making money, but we wasn't making but a dollar and forty cents a night. That's what we meant, we didn't get a dollar and forty cents a night. Which is, somewhere about 10 pips that week. Which thing was pretty tight, you know. And, uh, there they are. Somehow or other, Henry Horton and the man, got some misunderstanding between them two, I don't know what it was all about. The man got rid of Henry Horton, and the band wouldn't walk off with Henry Horton. So they turned the band over to me. Henry Horton, and the man, Henry Horton, and his rhythm kept shaking. Well, I took the band, and got me being the oldest man in the band. And the guys all knew I was, I was a Henry Horton long and then, he turned the band over to me, you know. And the other guy was telling me, and he turned the band over to me, you know. Well, Gilbert Young was playing something myself. And, we were skimming, Bartley was on the saxophone. And, you know, your house was on the saxophone. I think, and the old woman was on the saxophone. Papa, that boy you asked me about, called him Holly Papa?
